about.title: West Covina Wrongful Death Claims
about.longDescription: Losing someone suddenly leaves a family sorting through grief and paperwork at the same time. In West Covina, a city of about 108,484 people in Los Angeles County, public records show 5 traffic deaths in 2025 alongside 409 injury collisions. Each of those numbers is a household changed forever. The corridors with the highest collision counts in those records are the routes residents use every day: I-10 (San Bernardino Freeway), Azusa Avenue, Sunset Avenue and Amar Road. Not every wrongful death involves a vehicle, though. A fall at a workplace, a defective product, or negligent care can also give rise to a claim. Under California law, a wrongful death case is a civil action brought by the spouse or domestic partner and children first, then certain dependents or heirs. It runs separately from any criminal prosecution and generally must be filed within two years of the date of death, with a shorter window when a public agency is involved. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect West Covina families, free of charge, with an independent attorney who handles these cases on contingency.

whyChoose.title: Why West Covina Families Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Clarity on who is allowed to file
items.desc: California limits standing in wrongful death cases, giving priority to the surviving spouse or domestic partner and children, then certain dependents and heirs. An attorney in our network can explain where your family fits before anything is filed.

items.title: Deadlines tracked from day one
items.desc: Most claims must be brought within two years of the date of death, and the window shrinks considerably when a city, county, or state agency may be responsible. Early contact helps preserve those rights.

items.title: A separate civil path, no upfront cost
items.desc: A wrongful death claim proceeds independently of any criminal case and can seek funeral and burial costs, lost financial support, and the loss of love, companionship and guidance. Network attorneys work on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.question: My family member died in a crash on the I-10 in West Covina. Does it matter that the freeway is a state highway?
items.answer: It can. If part of the claim involves a public entity such as Caltrans, the City of West Covina, or Los Angeles County, California requires a government claim to be filed much sooner than the usual two-year deadline, often within months. An attorney can review the collision report and determine whether any public agency is involved so that no deadline is missed.

items.question: The other driver is facing criminal charges. Do we have to wait for that case to finish?
items.answer: No. A wrongful death claim is a civil action and moves on its own track, regardless of whether prosecutors file charges or how a criminal case ends. Many families pursue both at once. The civil case focuses on your family's losses rather than on punishment.

items.question: What can a wrongful death claim actually cover for our family?
items.answer: California law allows recovery of funeral and burial expenses, the financial support your loved one would have provided, and the loss of their love, companionship, and guidance. The exact figures depend on your family's circumstances, and no one can promise a particular result. An attorney will walk through what applies in your situation.
